newsitem.title: USA: Calif official tells Golden Eagle to boost reserve.
newsitem.headline: Calif official tells Golden Eagle to boost reserve.

text.p: California's Insurance Commissioner has issued an order directing San Diego-based Golden Eagle Insurance Co to increase its reserves by $138.5 million, the Insurance Department said.
The ordered followed an Insurance Department financial examination of the company.

According to the examination, the company's statutory surplus as of December 31, 1995 was $81.6 million. Based on current premium volume through the first six months of this year, the company's annualized premium to surplus ratio is 5.8 to 1, far in excess of industry standard, the department said.

The report concluded that the company's surplus of $81.6 million does not reasonably support the level of business underwritten by the company and that the net estimated loss reserve deficiencies totaled $138.5 million.
Golden Eagle, which is privately held, is the state's third-largest workers compensation insurer. In a statement, the company said it believes its reserves are adequate.
"Insurance Commissioner (Chuck) Quackenbush and his financial division have decided to try to slow us down," Golden Eagle said in a statement.
"In an attempt to do that, they chose to challenge our reserves for losses and loss adjustment expenses," the company said. "They are dead wrong."

Under the terms of the Insurance Department order, the company must remedy the reserve deficiency by November 15, 1996 and provide evidence to the commissioner's satisfaction before October 7 that the funds will be available for deposit by November 15.

On September 20, a San Francisco Superior Court Judge will hear arguments as to whether the Insurance Department should have held a public hearing before announcing the results of its Golden Eagle examination.
